newsitem.title: USA: ADM ethanol incentives a tax issue -- Glickman.
newsitem.headline: ADM ethanol incentives a tax issue -- Glickman.

text.p: Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman on Thursday said it was unlikely Archer Daniels Midland Co would lose its government tax incentives for ethanol producers.
"The ethanol subsidies...are tax-incentives available to everyone within a class,' Glickman said, saying this meant the government could not take them away from just one company.

"The programs...are by and large subject to the general provisions of the internal revenue code (for) which they are or are not eligible based on those circumstances, nothing we have anything to do with," he said during a question and answer session after a speech to the Washington Research Group.
"But what we can do, although we haven't made this judgement, is to determine their (ADM's) eligibility to participate in direct USDA programs like surplus commodity programs," Glickman added.

ADM pleaded guilty in October to two counts of fixing the prices of lysine, a feed additive, and citric acid, an additive in food, beverages and other products. As part of a plea agreement, it must pay $100 million in fines.
USDA said previously it was considering whether to bar ADM from federal prograams following the company's guilty plea.
